content:
CarPlay can make any car feel more comfortable and convenient. However, the out-of-the-box experience isn't always perfect.

Some models still require a wired connection, and some don't support CarPlay at all, let alone charge and cool your iPhone on long trips.

Fortunately, improving these issues doesn't require a large investment. The affordable accessories introduced below cover wireless CarPlay, MagSafe charging, cable management, and even adding a complete screen to older cars.

Converting wired CarPlay to wireless

If your vehicle already supports wired CarPlay, the Carlinkit Mini Ultra 3 lets you ditch the cable while retaining your car's touchscreen, steering wheel controls, built-in microphone, and factory sound system.

This compact adapter features both USB-A and USB-C ports. After the initial pairing, it automatically reconnects every time you start the car. It also supports wireless Android Auto on Android 11 or later, making it especially useful for vehicles shared between iPhone and Android users.

One thing to note: this adapter requires your car to already have wired CarPlay factory-installed — it cannot add this functionality to vehicles that don't support CarPlay.

The Carlinkit Mini Ultra 3 is currently on sale for $43.99 with Prime shipping.

Adding CarPlay to almost any older vehicle

For vehicles without CarPlay, installing a portable screen is usually the simplest upgrade option. The Krunia 9.26-inch portable CarPlay screen, priced at $89.99, adds wireless CarPlay without requiring you to remove the factory stereo.

The screen supports Bluetooth, AUX, and FM audio connections, and is compatible with Siri, Android Auto, and OTA firmware updates. The accessory also includes a backup camera, though installing the camera requires running a cable to the rear of the car.

For those who want CarPlay but don't want to replace their factory head unit, this is a rather attractive compromise.

Installing a permanent CarPlay head unit

A portable screen may not suit every dashboard. For a cleaner, permanent installation, consider the BOSS Audio BVCP9700A — an affordable double-DIN head unit with a 7-inch touchscreen that supports Apple CarPlay, Android Auto, Bluetooth, and a backup camera.

The unit is priced at $164.99. However, buyers should confirm compatibility with their vehicle before ordering. Installation kits, wiring harnesses, steering wheel control adapters, or professional installation services may add extra costs.

Cooling your iPhone while charging

Wireless charging, navigation running, sunlight, and a hot dashboard can create harsh conditions for your iPhone. The ESR CryoBoost MagSafe car charger has a built-in cooling fan to address this. It combines a magnetic vent or dashboard mount, wireless charging, and active cooling. At $29.99, it's especially suited for drivers using wireless CarPlay who still want to charge their iPhone on long trips.

A minimalist MagSafe mount without charging

Not every drive requires wireless charging. The standard ESR MagSafe car mount holds your iPhone on the dashboard or vent without needing additional charging cables.

Priced at $15.99, it includes a metal ring sticker for phones or cases that don't natively support magnetic attachment. In hot weather, charging generates extra heat, so switching to this mount may be a better choice.

Replacing unreliable CarPlay cables

Many CarPlay issues ultimately come down to cable wear or poor contact. The Anker Nano USB-A to USB-C CarPlay cable offers a braided data cable for newer USB-C iPhones, priced at $11.99.

Drivers using an iPhone 14 or older model can opt for Anker's PowerLine Flow USB-A to Lightning cable, priced at $17.99.

Adding fast charging for the best experience

USB ports that support wired CarPlay often charge slowly. The Anker 323 car charger plugs into the 12V power socket and provides one USB-C port and one USB-A port.

Priced at $14.99, it's an economical option for charging passengers' phones or powering other accessories. It won't interfere with your car's CarPlay connection, and it can speed up your own charging when used with wireless CarPlay.

Tidying up your installation

A $6.99 box of adhesive cable clips can make a portable CarPlay screen or wired phone mount installation look much neater. These clips route cables along the edges of the dashboard, keeping them out of the way of the gear shifter, pedals, and cup holders.

Using CarPlay doesn't require buying a new car or undertaking a major stereo upgrade. Depending on what your vehicle already has, spending anywhere from $12 on a better cable to about $90 on a complete portable screen can make daily use considerably more convenient.

Want to get even more out of CarPlay? Check out 9to5Mac's continuously updated list of over 120 iPhone apps that support CarPlay.
